facts.text: Paradero Todos Santos is located between Todos Santos and Pescadero on the Baja California Sur coast of Mexico.

facts.text: Three airports (Los Cabos SJD, La Paz LAP and Cabo San Lucas CSL) are each approximately one hour away.

facts.text: The hotel is defined by the five distinct ecosystems that surround it.
facts.excerpt: defined by the five distinct ecosystems that surround it and the ancient rituals shaped over generations

facts.text: Paradero Hotel is an adults-exclusive hotel.
facts.excerpt: Paradero Hotel is adults-only.

facts.text: Every suite has a private terrace, an indoor-outdoor rain shower, air conditioning, Wi-Fi, blackout drapes and an in-room safe.
facts.excerpt: Every suite has a private terrace, indoor-outdoor rain shower, A/C, Wi-Fi, blackout drapes, and an in-room safe.

facts.text: Both Sky Suites have private rooftop terraces with suspended stargazing nets.
facts.excerpt: Both Sky Suite variants have private rooftop terraces with suspended star nets

facts.text: The Mountain View Sky Suite faces the Sierra de la Laguna, farmland and the ocean horizon.
facts.excerpt: The Mountain View faces the Sierra de la Laguna, farmland, and the ocean horizon.

facts.text: The Saguaro Suite spans three levels on a corner lot with views of the Sierra de la Laguna mountains, Las Palmas Beach and the La Mesa farming fields.
facts.excerpt: A corner position that produces views unavailable from anywhere else on the property: the Sierra de la Laguna mountains, Las Palmas Beach, and La Mesa farming fields simultaneously.

facts.text: The ground-floor Garden Suite Hammock opens onto a Japanese-inspired desert zen garden with an artisan-made hammock.
facts.excerpt: The Garden Suite Hammock (640 sq ft) is ground-floor, opening onto a Japanese-inspired desert zen garden with an artisan hammock.

facts.text: The Garden Suite Soak Tub has an outdoor soaking tub on its ground-floor terrace within the zen garden.
facts.excerpt: Only the Garden Suite Soak Tub. The tub sits on the ground-floor terrace within the zen garden.

facts.text: The Garden Suite design draws from Mexican hacienda heritage and Japanese spatial minimalism.
facts.excerpt: The design draws from both Mexican hacienda heritage and Japanese spatial minimalism.

facts.text: The Ojo de Agua Spa draws on the healing traditions of Mexico and the stillness of the Baja landscape.
facts.excerpt: we invite you to relax at our Ojo de Agua Spa. Where practices and services draw from the healing traditions of Mexico and the stillness of the Baja landscape.

facts.text: A traditional temazcal and sound healing are complimentary for Paradero Unbound guests.
facts.excerpt:
Complimentary experiences for Paradero Unbound guests

facts.text: The all-inclusive Paradero Unbound rate includes breakfast, lunch and dinner, access to experiences, breathwork, sound healing and horseback riding.
facts.excerpt: Destination-driven dining, immersive experiences, and transportation are thoughtfully included.

facts.text: Dining uses local ingredients sourced from the hotel's living milpa, which helps restore Baja's native ecosystem.
facts.excerpt: With local ingredients sourced from our living milpa that helps restore Baja

facts.text: Experiences are land-led journeys across the five ecosystems that surround Paradero.
facts.excerpt: Land-led journeys across the five ecosystems that surround Paradero, guided by rituals shaped over generations.

facts.text: Architects Ruben Valdez and Yashar Yektajo designed desert-hued, brutalist-inflected structures around a 100,000-square-foot botanical garden of endemic plants.
facts.excerpt: The result is a series of desert-hued, brutalist-inflected structures that surround a 100,000-square-foot botanical garden where endemic plants like red sand verbena, Mojave yucca, and Shaw

facts.text: The hotel is not beachfront; the Pacific is a solid hike or short drive away.
facts.excerpt: The hotel isn’t beachfront, like many in the area are, but rather a solid hike or short drive to the Pacific.

facts.text: The Ojo de Agua spa has hot and cold dipping pools and is shaded by almost 100 palm trees.
facts.excerpt: Shaded by almost 100 palm trees and other endemic plants, the Ojo de Agua (watering hole) spa has hot and cold dipping pools.

facts.text: Rooms have no TVs or phones, and there is no room service.
facts.excerpt: The rooms don’t have TVs, or even phones to call for room service (they don’t offer it).

facts.text: The property has an infinity pool and an open-air common area called the living room, with hammocks and rattan lounge pillows.
facts.excerpt: the spa, infinity pool, and the open-air common area known as the living room (hammocks, rattan lounge pillows)

facts.text: The restaurant is led by chef Eduardo Rios, an alum of Pujol in Mexico City.
facts.excerpt: Led by chef Eduardo Ríos—an alum of Enrique Olvera’s Mexico City restaurant, Pujol—the restaurant turns out classic seafood dishes like chocolata clams and fried soft shell crab tacos.

facts.text: Pets are welcome with prior notice to the reservations team and applicable charges.
facts.excerpt: Pets are welcome with prior notice to the reservations team and applicable charges.
